findings.title: OAuth, linked identity, recovery, and ranked identity
Device lineage, challenge, replay, checkpoint, and recovery
Local daemon, shell, IPC, and platform supervision
Universal adapter certification and deterministic accounting
Ranking authorization, immutable generations, periods, and corrections
Social relationships, boards, presence, and notifications
Export, deletion, retention, and backup tombstones
Release authorization, compatibility, migration, and rollback
Current-authorization recheck at every display and delivery boundary

restatement.previous_form: Privacy-safe projection and current authorization, stated as a repairable cluster with no artifact set of its own.
restatement.rationale: Independent review found no independent artifact set: the aggregates named in the original wording are already owned by SR-010, SR-011 and SR-013, so the finding could not be closed by repairing anything it exclusively owned. It is restated as the invariant it actually asserts - every display and delivery boundary rechecks current authorization instead of replaying a historical snapshot - and bound to the boundary operations where that recheck is absent today. The artifact set intentionally intersects SR-010, SR-011 and SR-013 at different sites: those findings own their aggregates, this one owns the boundary. Closure is one enumerated boundary matrix plus a current-authorization check at every listed boundary, and is not satisfied by repairing any single aggregate.

findings.title: Review-record integrity: reviewed head, evidence class, and named owners

restatement.previous_form: Review, conformance, and launch-evidence integrity, owned by the document that states the finding.
restatement.rationale: The finding was self-owned: its normative owners were the semantic-review document that states it and the schema inventory, so its closure evidence would have been the same prose that defines it and no external record could contradict it. Ownership moves to the two machine records that own reviewed-head and evidence-class facts, and the prose review documents become conflicting artifacts. The disagreement is now machine-checkable: REPAIR_HEAD_REVIEW.md pins e1320a6, the semantic review states base 41ecb77, and review-target-v1.json is not-pinned with a null commit; separately the state-machine registry names persistence owners for 19 of its 26 machines that packages/schemas/planning-schema.sql does not define. Closure is a pinned review-target-v1.json whose commit exists and whose verdict is recorded, prose head claims equal to it, suite names that match what each suite executes, and one resolved persistence owner for every registered machine.

findings.title: Source-bound evidence and verifier appraisal authority

restatement.previous_form: Stated as a contradiction whose closure required four unwritten schemas, with an artifact set that named nothing existing.
restatement.rationale: Independent review found that authoring an absent schema is a design task rather than a disagreement between two authorities, so the finding as written could not be falsified. It is split into the two things it actually contains. The contradiction part is live and now cited: one appraisal aggregate is described three ways - vibeproof-claim-v1.cddl verifier-appraisal-v1 carries seven classification dimensions, evidence-profile-policy-v1.json enumerates the same seven dimensions as server-verifier authority, and planning-schema.sql verifier_appraisals persists only provenance, continuity and integrity state with no claim digest, evidence digest, validity interval or supersession. The design part is the four artifacts already recorded planned-missing in SCHEMA_AND_INTERFACE_INVENTORY.md; they move to planned_artifacts, because a path that does not exist cannot be cited as a conflicting artifact. Closure requires both halves: the three existing authorities agree on one appraisal record, and the four planned artifacts exist and bind the exact claim, evidence, policy and result under D-077.
